title: Vim
label: Vim
desc: Modal text editor where edits are commands composed from an operator and a motion.

sections.title: Setup
sections.description: Install Vim, confirm what the build supports, and open files with the cursor already placed.

snippets.code:
# Check the version and the feature list first
vim --version | head -n 3

# Debian and Ubuntu install a minimal vim-tiny by default
sudo apt install vim

# macOS ships an old binary; Homebrew keeps a current one
brew install vim

# Windows
winget install --id vim.vim -e

# Start on line 42 of a file
vim +42 notes.md

# Read-only session, saving needs an explicit bang
vim -R report.txt

# One tab page per file
vim -p src/main.rs src/lib.rs tests/render.rs

# Skip every vimrc and plugin for this session only
vim --clean notes.md

sections.title: Modes
sections.description: Normal mode is home; every other mode is a short visit that Escape ends.

snippets.code:
Normal      keys are commands, not text; Escape returns here
Insert      i a o O I A, Escape goes back
Visual      v by character, V by line, Ctrl-v by block
Replace     R overwrites, gR keeps the layout of the text
Command     : opens the ex line, / and ? open a search
Terminal    :terminal runs a shell inside a window

" Run one Normal command without leaving Insert
<C-o>dd

" Type a character by its decimal code point
<C-v>233

" While still in Insert: delete a word, then paste a register
<C-w>
<C-r>0

sections.title: Moving
sections.description: Motions accept a count, so a few keystrokes cover long distances.

snippets.code:
h j k l     " one character left, down, up, right
w b e       " next word start, previous word start, word end
ge          " end of the previous word
0 ^ $       " first column, first non-blank, end of line
g_          " last non-blank character

3w          " three words forward
12j         " twelve lines down

gg          " first line of the buffer
G           " last line
42G         " line 42, same as :42 and 42gg
%           " matching bracket
{  }        " previous and next paragraph
H  M  L     " top, middle and bottom of the screen

<C-d> <C-u> " half a screen down and up
<C-f> <C-b> " a full screen down and up
zz          " centre the cursor line

sections.title: Editing
sections.description: Operators wait for a motion or a text object, so one grammar covers every change.

snippets.code:
dw      " delete to the next word
d2w     " delete two words
d$      " delete to the end of the line, same as D
dd      " delete the whole line
3dd     " delete three lines

cw      " change to the end of the word
cc      " change the whole line, same as S
C       " change to the end of the line

yy      " yank the line
p       " paste after the cursor or below the line
P       " paste before
x       " delete the character under the cursor, same as dl
X       " delete the character before the cursor
r-      " overwrite one character with a dash
~       " swap the case of one character
J       " join the next line, with one space

" The last change can be replayed wherever the cursor lands
ciw     " change the word under the cursor
report  " type the replacement, then press Escape
w       " move to the next word
.       " apply the same change there

u       " undo the last change
<C-r>   " redo it

sections.title: Visual Mode
sections.description: Select first, then run an operator on exactly what is highlighted.

snippets.code:
v       " character-wise selection
V       " line-wise selection
<C-v>   " block selection
gv      " reselect the last selection
o       " move the cursor to the other end

d  y  c " delete, yank or change the selection
>  <    " indent or outdent; the dot command repeats it

" Block insert: comment out the next three lines
<C-v>jjI// <Esc>

" Block append: a semicolon at the end of each line
<C-v>jjA;<Esc>

" Replace every selected character with a dash
<C-v>jjr-

" A visual selection is also a range for ex commands
:'<,'>normal A;      " append a semicolon to each line
:'<,'>sort           " sort the selected lines
:'<,'>!column -t     " pipe the lines through an external filter

sections.title: Search
sections.description: A search is a motion, so every command that takes a motion also takes a match.

snippets.code:
/pattern    " search forward
?pattern    " search backward
n           " next match in the same direction
N           " previous match
*           " search the word under the cursor, forwards
#           " the same word, backwards
g*          " like *, but also matches inside longer words

:set incsearch           " preview the match while typing
:set hlsearch            " keep every match highlighted
:nohlsearch              " clear the highlight until the next search
:set ignorecase smartcase   " lowercase finds any case, capitals narrow it

/error\c                 " ignore case for this pattern only
/error\C                 " force case sensitivity

" Matches work as the right-hand side of an operator
d/end       " delete up to the next occurrence of end
c?begin     " change back to the previous begin

" Park the cursor on the last character of the match
/function/e

sections.title: Replace
sections.description: Substitute acts on a range, and the range defaults to the current line.

snippets.code:
:s/teh/the/         " first occurrence on this line
:s/teh/the/g        " every occurrence on this line
:%s/teh/the/g       " every line in the buffer
:%s/teh/the/gc      " ask before each replacement
:5,20s/teh/the/g    " only lines 5 to 20

" Trailing whitespace, silently, across the whole file
:%s/\s\+$//e

" Swap two comma-separated fields with very magic mode
:%s/\v(\w+), (\w+)/\2 \1/g

" An empty pattern reuses the last search
:%s//replacement/g

" A carriage return in the replacement splits the line
:%s/; /\r/g

sections.title: Registers
sections.description: Every delete and yank lands in a register; a quote in front of the command picks which one.

snippets.code:
:registers          " every register and its contents
"ayy                " yank this line into register a
"ap                 " paste register a after the cursor
"Ayy                " append this line to register a

yy                  " a yank also lands in register 0
p                   " paste from the unnamed register
"0p                 " paste the last yank, even after a delete

"+y     " the system clipboard, needs +clipboard
"+p     " paste from the system clipboard
"*y     " the X11 primary selection on Linux
"_dd    " the black hole, leaves other registers untouched
"-p     " the small delete register, for deletes under a line
"1p     " the newest of the numbered delete registers

" Put text into a register from an expression
:let @a = "reviewed"
"ap                 " paste reviewed

" The expression register evaluates what you type
<C-r>=2*21<CR>      " insert 42 while in Insert mode
:put =strftime('%Y-%m-%d')   " insert today's date on a new line

sections.title: Macros
sections.description: A macro is a register full of keystrokes, recorded once and replayed anywhere.

snippets.code:
qa          " record into register a
A;<Esc>     " append a semicolon, then leave Insert
j           " move down one line
q           " stop recording

@a          " replay the macro once
@@          " replay the last macro again
5@a         " replay it five times

" A macro is text, so it can be edited like text
:put a              " dump register a into the buffer
" edit the keys, select only those lines, then yank them back
"ay                 " store the selection in register a

:%normal @a         " run the macro on every line

sections.title: Buffers
sections.description: A buffer is the file in memory; a window is only a viewport onto it.

snippets.code:
:ls                 " list open buffers with numbers and flags
:e notes.md         " load a file into a new buffer
:b 3                " switch to buffer number 3
:b notes            " switch to the buffer whose name matches notes
:bn  :bp            " next and previous buffer
:bfirst  :blast     " first and last buffer
<C-^>               " toggle to the alternate buffer

:bd                 " unload this buffer, keep the window open
:bd 3 5             " unload buffers 3 and 5
:bwipeout           " remove the buffer together with its marks
:bufdo %s/TODO/DONE/ge | update   " edit every buffer and save it

sections.title: Windows
sections.description: Splits inside one tab page share the same list of buffers.

snippets.code:
:sp                 " horizontal split on the same buffer
:vs notes.md        " vertical split with another file
<C-w>s  <C-w>v      " the same two commands from Normal mode
<C-w>w              " cycle through the windows
<C-w>h  <C-w>j  <C-w>k  <C-w>l   " move by direction
<C-w>q              " close the current window
<C-w>o              " keep only this window

<C-w>=              " equalise width and height
<C-w>_              " maximise the height of this window
<C-w>|              " maximise its width
:resize 24          " height of 24 rows
:vertical resize 100   " width of 100 columns

<C-w>r              " rotate the windows
<C-w>x              " exchange this window with the next
<C-w>T              " move this window into its own tab

sections.title: Tabs
sections.description: A tab page is a layout of windows, not a file.

snippets.code:
:tabnew             " an empty tab page
:tabe src/main.rs   " open a file in a new tab
gt  gT              " next and previous tab
2gt                 " the second tab
:tabs               " list the open tab pages
:tabclose           " close the current tab
:tabonly            " close every other tab

:tabmove 0              " move this tab to the front
:tabmove                " move it to the end
:tabdo %s/foo/bar/ge    " substitute in every tab
:tab split              " copy the current window into a new tab

sections.title: Marks
sections.description: Marks remember positions, so you can leave a file and return to the exact spot.

snippets.code:
ma          " mark this line as a
`a          " jump to the exact column of mark a
'a          " jump to the first non-blank of that line
:marks      " list every mark and its target
``          " the position before the last jump
`.          " the line of the last change

mA          " uppercase marks are global, across files
`A          " open the file and jump to mark A

'[  ']      " start and end of the last change or yank
g;  g,      " walk the change list backwards and forwards
<C-o> <C-i> " walk the jump list backwards and forwards
:delmarks a " forget one lowercase mark
:delmarks!  " forget every lowercase mark

sections.title: Ex Commands
sections.description: The colon line edits by address, and Normal mode commands can be replayed over a range.

snippets.code:
:1,10d          " delete lines 1 to 10
:.,$d           " delete from here to the end
:%y             " yank the whole buffer
:5,15normal A;  " append a semicolon to lines 5 to 15
:g/^#/d         " delete every line that starts with a hash
:v/TODO/d       " delete every line that does not contain TODO

:r !date +%F        " insert today's date below the cursor
:r !ls -1           " insert a directory listing
:!make test         " run a shell command and show its output
:terminal           " a shell in a window, leave it with exit
:earlier 10m        " go back ten minutes in the undo tree

" Addresses accept marks and search patterns
:'a,'bd             " the lines between marks a and b
:/begin/,/end/d     " from the next begin to the next end

" Save a copy and keep editing the original
:saveas draft.md

sections.title: Configuration
sections.description: The vimrc is a script run at startup: options, mappings and autocommands live there.

snippets.code:
" Ask Vim which file it actually loaded
:echo $MYVIMRC
:edit $MYVIMRC
:source $MYVIMRC    " apply it without restarting

" Windows reads $HOME\_vimrc instead of ~/.vimrc
:edit ~/_vimrc

set nocompatible
filetype plugin indent on
syntax on

set number relativenumber
set cursorline
set scrolloff=6
set ignorecase smartcase
set incsearch hlsearch
set expandtab shiftwidth=4 softtabstop=4
set undofile
set signcolumn=yes
set mouse=a

let mapleader = " "          " space; declare it before any mapping

nnoremap <leader>w :write<CR>
nnoremap <leader>e :edit $MYVIMRC<CR>
inoremap jk <Esc>
xnoremap <leader>y "+y

augroup trim_trailing_whitespace
  autocmd!
  autocmd BufWritePre *.rs,*.py,*.md keeppatterns %s/\s\+$//e
augroup END

sections.title: Plugins
sections.description: Vim has a package loader built in; vim-plug adds fetching, updating and cleanup commands.

snippets.code:
# One-time install of the plugin manager
curl -fLo ~/.vim/autoload/plug.vim --create-dirs \
  https://raw.githubusercontent.com/junegunn/vim-plug/master/plug.vim

:PlugInstall      " fetch everything declared in the vimrc
:PlugUpdate       " update the installed plugins
:PlugClean        " remove plugins no longer declared
:PlugStatus       " what is installed and what is missing
:PlugDiff         " review the changes from the last update
